absent: Locking and lifetime rules for dump position counters and mapping metadata beyond the read side and sequence protection shown.
Filesystem specific write iterator and seek contracts beyond the mode capability checks shown.
Layouts and valid ranges for task and mount and dentry and register view structures referenced but not defined here.
Interruption and scheduling semantics for dump cancellation and register writeback callbacks.
Callers and recovery for note sizing failures and omitted process wide notes beyond the shown return flags.
Accounting and notification effects for dump writes beyond the modification and counter updates shown for iterator writes.

findings.text: Kernel iterator writes are permitted only for files marked writable and capable of writing and that expose an iterator without a conflicting plain write handler. Successful writes update the caller position from the synchronous control block and signal modification and record write accounting while misuse yields descriptor or argument errors.
Seeking is permitted only for files marked seekable and otherwise fails as nonseekable. Permitted seeks are delegated to the filesystem handler for the requested offset and origin.

Path strings for synthetic objects may come from a custom dentry formatter unless the dentry is a normally mounted root with unlinked objects visibly marked. Otherwise the rendered string is built backwards into caller storage relative to the current root and length failures are reported distinctly.
File path rendering is equivalent to generic path rendering applied to the stored file location using caller storage.
A mount belongs to the fail filesystem exactly when its superblock identity matches the fail filesystem root superblock.
Alignment requests must be powers of two. The helper defers enough padding to align the logical dump position including already deferred bytes.
Dump skipping preserves logical position either by seeking when supported with interruption awareness or by emitting zero pages in bounded pieces when seeking is unavailable.

Generated core headers are mutually consistent core images for the supplied machine and flags with coherent identity and versioning and type and sizing and segment count. Accompanying note descriptors describe only a file extent with neutral addressing and a fixed small alignment.
A note descriptor associates owner name with numeric type and payload extent and payload location. A short token helper supplies the conventional owner and type pair.

Status notes reflect the fatal signal and pending and held masks and hierarchical identity numbers and timing that is group wide for leaders and per task otherwise together with accumulated child times.

Process info notes reflect truncated and normalized command line arguments and hierarchical identity numbers and decoded scheduling state with zombie indication and scheduling and flag state and protected owner identifiers and short command name.
Auxiliary notes expose saved vectors through their terminator and signal notes expose externally formatted fatal signal details.

File notes list only file backed mappings with count and page granularity and per mapping extent and offset and path strings. Total size honors overflow and administrative bounds with growth and retry on pathname length pressure and compaction when estimates overcount.

Reverse buffers start at the end of caller storage with overflow latched as a negative remainder. Extraction fails on overflow and single character extension either consumes space or latches overflow.

Component extension is a no-op once overflowed and otherwise preserves as much trailing content as fits while latching overflow on shortage. Kernel memory copying substitutes placeholders on fault and name handling safely samples volatile name storage before adding a separator.

Path assembly terminates as complete or at absolute root or detached or unattached or on hierarchy escape while crossing mount roots into parents. It guarantees a root separator when no component was emitted.
Path sampling and traversal run under read side protection with restart on rename or mount generation change. Filesystem root sampling uses its own sequence protection.
Core note identity and credential fields are sampled under read side protection with atomic single reads for concurrently mutated state.

Per thread dumps form a chain carrying task identity with embedded status and variable trailing notes. Collective note state carries the chain with process wide notes and external signal storage and total sized extent and per thread capacity.
Optional register writeback may run for the dumped task with status extent equal to its record size and floating point presence recorded as validity on the status.

With a register view the primary set populates the embedded status register area and always yields a status note while further sets yield notes only when marked for core inclusion and active. Dynamic payloads carry validity marking for floating state with defaulted and validated ownership and accumulated sizing.

Without a register view general state always yields a status note and floating state yields an additional note only when allocation and capture both succeed. Otherwise the second note is silently omitted while validity reflects success.
Task register capture uses an architecture hook when present and otherwise performs a generic state copy guarded by a size consistency expectation.

Collection determines machine and flags and per thread capacity from the register view or architecture defaults with memory derived override and prepares the header. It instantiates the dumper membership chain and populates all threads for the fatal signal and sizes process wide notes while tolerating omission of file mappings.
Emission requires every present note to be written with process wide notes accompanying the first thread and remaining thread notes following. Any single write failure aborts the whole emission.
Teardown assumes the primary thread note aliases embedded status and releases only separately allocated thread payloads with thread records and process wide variable payloads.
Extended numbering uses a single null section that conveys the true segment total while the header points at it with consistent linkage.

Insufficient pathname space is a length failure rather than silent truncation with generic rendering latching overflow and file note building growing and retrying. Absent pathnames simply omit entries and may yield empty notes.

Mode capability mismatches produce distinct descriptor or argument or pipe errors depending on the operation. Dump advancement switches between seeking and zero emission based on seek capability and interruption state.

ABI facts include core type ET_CORE and note type PT_NOTE with alignment four and auxiliary terminator AT_NULL and null section type SHT_NULL with undefined string index SHN_UNDEF and SEEK_CUR relative skipping.
Note handling moves from sized collection to ordered emission to selective release with emission gated on collection success and release limited to independently allocated storage.
